test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 05 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In May 2025, which among the following institutions formally announced the creation of the Payments Regulatory Board (PRB), a six-member panel responsible for overseeing the country’s payment systems?

options.text: Securities and Exchange Board of India
Small Industries Development Bank of India
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development

solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** announced the formation of the **Payments Regulatory Board (PRB)** in May 2025. The PRB is a six-member panel entrusted with the responsibility of overseeing and regulating the country's payment systems.
 
• The **Payments Regulatory Board** was established as per the recommendations of the **Committee on Digital Payments**, headed by **Ratan Watal**. This committee emphasized the need for a separate regulatory body for payment systems in India.
 
• The PRB's objectives include ensuring the development of secure, efficient, and accessible payment systems while promoting innovation and competition in the payment ecosystem.
 
• The six-member PRB comprises the **Governor of the RBI** as the Chairperson, a Deputy Governor of the RBI as a member, and nominees from the Central Government, along with independent experts in the field of payment systems.
 
• The establishment of the PRB aligns with the RBI's role in fostering a robust and secure digital payment infrastructure, which is critical for the country's digital economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**

 
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India** is India's central bank, established on **April 1, 1935**, under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**.
 
• It is headquartered in **Mumbai**, Maharashtra, and primarily functions to regulate the issue of currency and manage the country's monetary policy.
 
• The RBI plays a crucial role in supervising and regulating banks, fostering financial stability, and promoting the development of financial markets.
 
 
 
• **Committee on Digital Payments:**
 
 
• The **Ratan Watal Committee** was constituted by the Government of India in **2016** to suggest measures to increase the use of digital payments.
 
• It recommended the establishment of a dedicated regulatory body for payment systems to ensure better governance and oversight.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Payments Regulatory Board:**
 
 
• Regulating payment systems in India to ensure their security, efficiency, and accessibility.
 
• Promoting competition and innovation in the payment ecosystem.
 
• Ensuring the protection of consumer interests in the digital payment space.
 
• Monitoring the compliance of payment service providers with regulatory norms and guidelines.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Payment Systems Regulation:**
 
 
• A robust payment system infrastructure ensures **secure and efficient transactions**, fostering trust in the digital economy.
 
• Regulation helps in mitigating risks such as **frauds, cyberattacks, and operational failures** in payment systems.
 
• It promotes financial inclusion by enabling easier access to digital payment methods for underserved populations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The RBI is responsible for overseeing the country's payment systems under the **Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007**.
 
• The establishment of the PRB was a significant step to ensure the growth of a **secure, seamless, and innovative payment ecosystem** in India.
 
• The PRB's formation reflects India's commitment to strengthening its digital payment infrastructure, which is pivotal to achieving a **cashless economy**.
 
• Global examples, such as the **Payment Systems Regulator (PSR)** in the UK, have demonstrated the benefits of having a separate regulatory body for payment systems.
